description: Models the space of valid Ramsey R(5,5) graphs as the ground states of an infinite-range spin glass model where Hamiltonian corresponds to the count of monochromatic K5s. By studying the Lee-Yang-Fisher zeros of the partition function in the complex temperature plane, we can identify a thermodynamic phase transition that strictly demarcates the non-existence of valid graphs when N >= R(5,5).
mathematical_formalization: Z_N(\beta) = \sum_{x \in \{0,1\}^{\binom{N}{2}}} e^{-\beta H(x)}, where H(x) is the K5 count. The Lee-Yang zeros accumulate on the real axis at a critical size N_c = R(5,5).
analogical_connections: The disappearance of valid graphs at R(5,5) is analogous to the sudden loss of magnetization in a ferromagnetic material as it crosses the Curie temperature, or a phase boundary where zero-temperature entropy exactly hits zero.
implementation_hypothesis: Use simulated annealing and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) with parallel tempering to map out the density of states. Compute the partition function zeros using numerical analytic continuation. Track how the leading zero approaches the real axis as N grows.
experiment_seed: Estimate the partition function zeros for R(3,3)=6 and R(4,4)=18 first. Observe the scaling of zero locations. Then run an extrapolated scaling analysis up to N=46 to predict the R(5,5) boundary.
